references.text: Paul quotes directly from Deuteronomy 21:23 and applies it to Christ, who became a curse for us by hanging on the tree of the cross, to redeem us from the curse of the law.
Joshua followed the command to take down the body of the king of Ai from the tree before sunset and bury it, in accordance with the law that a body must not remain hanging on the tree overnight.
Joshua hanged the five kings on trees but took them down before sunset and placed them in a cave, obeying the command in Deuteronomy 21:23.
The Jews asked Pilate to ensure that the bodies would not remain on the cross on the Sabbath, reflecting the command that a body must not hang overnight.
Peter uses the expression 'hanged on a tree' to describe Jesus' crucifixion, linking it to the curse mentioned in Deuteronomy 21:23.
Peter describes Jesus' death as being hanged on a tree, a formulation that connects to the law's provision and the curse in Deuteronomy 21:23.
Paul notes that Jesus was taken down from the tree and laid in a tomb, in accordance with the command for burial on the same day.
Peter uses the expression 'on the tree' to refer to the cross where Christ bore our sins, linking this to the curse in Deuteronomy 21:23.
